text: Okay, proclamation. Whereas all people should have access to safe, healthy, and affordable homes within communities of opportunity and whereas housing stability and staying socially distant from those outside of our household has become our state's core public health strategy and whereas Governor Inslee has recognized the correlation between housing access and vulnerability and has extended a residential eviction moratorium through June 30th, 2021 to prevent families and individuals from losing their housing and whereas anyone, whereas everyone benefits from affordable housing, including the people who reside in these properties, their neighbors, businesses, employers, and the community as a whole and whereas the need for affordable homes across King County prior to the COVID-19 pandemic and the number of people experiencing homelessness has remained at crisis levels and whereas people, organizations, and communities throughout King County are participating in local affordable housing week to elevate the critical need to preserve and increase affordable housing in our communities and whereas the City of Renton endorses the goals, objectives, and purposes of affordable housing week and recommits itself to ensuring that our community recovers equitably from the crisis at hand and that all people live with dignity and safe, healthy, and affordable homes. Now, therefore, I, Armando Pavone, Mayor of the City of Renton, do hereby proclaim May 10th through 17th, 2021 to be affordable housing week in the City of Renton and I encourage all members of the community to join me in the special observation and witness whereof I'm here to set my hand and cause the seal of the City of Renton to be affixed this 10th day of May 2021. Signed, Armando Pavone, Mayor of the City of Renton. Mr. Mayor? Yes,

speaker: Other
text: speak this evening, Mr. Mayor. Okay. Is there anyone in the audience that would like to address Council? If so, please do so by raising your hand. And I see, oh, and I see one hand raised. Renton Chamber of Commerce. Go ahead. Good evening. Thank you very much. I'm Diane Dobson, the CEO for the Renton Chamber of Commerce. I'm also a Renton resident, and I come to you tonight in my capacity as the Chamber to make address to the Council as this platform is provided. Originally, I'd hoped to come to you tonight and invite you all to join in the Kindness Crawl scheduled for this weekend, an event celebrating our businesses downtown, encouraging collaborative partnerships of businesses and vendors from outside the downtown core popping up into our brick and mortars downtown for new experiences for those who are in downtown regularly and to expose some of those outside area vendors and businesses to our downtown core. A rising tide raises all ships. There have been generosity challenges promoting the event, random acts of kindness promotions with prizes that businesses sponsored, kindness bingo and commonality challenges, in addition to a magnificent opportunity to bring additional foot traffic to those businesses who are not just struck with COVID, but with businesses further impacted by the challenges of the downtown construction. The overarching theme was kindness, exhibiting kindness to yourself, to your neighbors, to your community. But in kindness to the participants, we've elected to postpone the event. Have you ever gone to a location, I use downtown Seattle as my own personal example, that isn't necessarily easy to get to, that causes confusion, has construction or congestion that's hard to navigate? For me personally, I often leave that destination saying to myself, well, that was a great event, but it was as difficult to get to as I imagined and I'm not going to do that again. And it then causes me further reluctance in visiting an area or location again. And that's what we decided to avoid with the event this weekend. I might be standalone with my sentiments in this room, but there are others that we've spoken with that would agree, including many of the downtown business owners who encouraged us to postpone as well. Now, I wouldn't ever anticipate the city to plan a construction schedule around an event. To the contrary, we planned our events around the construction schedule. And I know delays come up and challenges exist and are presented. And I'm kept abreast on those items as I choose to attend the bi-weekly meetings that the city provides for construction updates. I learned of the challenges as we missed the promised downtown deadline of April 1st. And I learned of more challenges when the April 12th date was suggested and then the end of April. And as we came nearer and nearer to the event date, I became more worried. Construction was still happening, confusion would exist. Coming from 30 years of law though, the liability that jumped out at me when I learned the project had experienced at least another two week delay and the sidewalks would be torn out this week and pedestrian traffic diverted into the street reduced down to one lane was enough liability exposure to say we need to postpone. Ladies and gentlemen, I don't come to you tonight to complain about the event postponement. In the world of COVID, delays happen more frequently than ever. But I do come to challenge the council on the construction downtown. These businesses have had over a year of construction and the light at the end of the tunnel has been dragged on and on and continually moved. And while your public works in engineering or do what they can to explain and appease, at some point we have to look at the processes. Is the lowest bid the best option when it seems there are quality control issues or thrown us missing and it causes a delay in the job? When it causes our general community to choose to go elsewhere because of the headache of construction or worse yet the damage to their vehicles they experience if they do try to come down, people will choose to go elsewhere. People are choosing to go elsewhere. Businesses report a bigger slowdown because of construction than from COVID. It's reported Uber Eats, DoorDash and other food delivery service drivers are refusing to pick up from restaurants downtown often leaving meals prepared and left at the restaurant. Businesses are tired. They're tired of reaching out of challenges they are experiencing and some items they shouldn't be burdened with reporting. Things like damage to their buildings or property. Things they now are tasked with follow-up on with their insurance, with repair shops, with reports to only be told the end is near. But then to learn of additional challenges and more postponements. I learned this morning that the sidewalks are being torn out in hopes that the concrete can be poured subsequent but because of the initial delay on the work, the concrete sub vendors have had to get involved in other jobs and the pour date remains as a tentative hopeful. We all know the streetscapes are going to be beautiful, walkable, vibrant and while many cities have been shut down, renting is receiving a facelift. But man it's getting tough to stay focused on that positive when the challenges continue to mount and our business continue to suffer. Please, I plead with you as a council, as administration to do what it takes to move this project along in front of these downtown businesses. Authorized night work, weekend work, hold contractors accountable to delays but we've got to do something. These businesses are suffering. Thank you very much for your time and your attention. I know the construction process and I'm learning is far more challenging than I ever anticipated but we've got to do something to step up as a city to support these businesses before more doors close. No one else, Mr. Mayor.
